_comment: Collection plan for the full Thai company universe, partitioned by registered capital (ทุนจดทะเบียน). Every set carries the same status/type constraint. Run sets in run_order: highest capital first, so the most valuable accounts land in the CRM earliest.

common_filters_meaning.jpStatusList: 1 = ยังดำเนินกิจการอยู่ (operating)
common_filters_meaning.jpTypeList: 5 = บริษัทจำกัด, 7 = บริษัทมหาชนจำกัด

set0_pilot.label: ทุน 5M-100,000M + รายได้ 100M+ + กำไร 10M+
set0_pilot.note: The April 2026 dataset, already migrated into the store. A subset of sets 1-3.

set6.label: ทุน 900k-1M
set6.note: Largest set by far. 1,000,000 baht is the default registered capital for Thai SMEs, so this single band is ~46% of the universe.

design_notes: Capital bands are non-overlapping by construction (each Min is the previous Max + 1), so sets 1-7 partition the universe exactly once on capital.

Sets 1-3 overlap set0 on capital, but the store merges on juristic_id, so re-fetching those rows is harmless - it updates last_seen_at and records any real change. The 'optimize to not intersect set0' idea is not worth implementing: the complement of (revenue>=100M AND profit>=10M) is (revenue<100M OR profit<10M), and the API filter model is AND-only, so it cannot be expressed as a single query.

Task 0.2 in the original plan (capital 5M-100,000M with revenue <100M and profit <10M) is made unnecessary by sets 1-3, which carry no revenue/profit filter and therefore already include those companies.

Sort order: the run_order itself delivers 'high to low'. Within a set, rows arrive partitioned by juristic-ID prefix rather than sorted globally, so a sortBy value does not change which companies are collected - only the order within a bucket. Sorting for presentation belongs in the export step, not the sweep.
Every set is swept using the same adaptive ID-prefix algorithm; only the capital filter changes.
